prompt:
David's Customer Engagement portfolio review is first thing Monday, and he wants my whole book walked in clean before it. It's been a rough few weeks, between the Sunbelt and Palmetto invoice mix-up, the Mosaic damage claim, and the coverage gap I flagged earlier that we never properly closed out, and I'd rather none of that land as a surprise in front of the team.

Take a pass through every deal I'm still carrying so we know exactly where each one stands and the CRM is telling the truth. The two April billing deals wrapped last week once the corrected invoices went out to the clients and the payment dates were confirmed, so they're settled and should be marked won rather than left open. Anything still genuinely mid-move stays exactly where it is; don't advance or close a deal just to make the list look tidier.

What David really wants is which account is closest to walking, and he's after the honest read, based on what actually happened to my book this month rather than a hunch. Once you've landed on it, add a clear risk note to that account in the CRM so the history's on record for whoever picks it up later, but leave the deal stage untouched and just add the note. Then lock in the call I already promised that client and never got onto the calendar, the one where I said David and I would both join alongside their side to walk it through, before it slips any further.

One of my clients also came back to me this week wanting to do more with us after how their first moves went, and I haven't set anything up for it yet. Tee it up as a new deal in the CRM so we don't lose that momentum.

Once all of that's done, email David the account-by-account rundown of where every deal stands and what I changed. Then post a short version in the team channel so the coordinators can see where each of my accounts sits going into Monday.

The damage, gap, and executive escalation are the load-bearing basis; the newest-client point is a supporting characterization a valid note may frame differently (e.g., highest-volume / most critical client), so it is not mandatory.
